q: How did Paul become an apostle?
a: Paul became an apostle through Jesus Christ and God the Father.

q: From what have believers in Jesus Christ been delivered?
a: Believers in Jesus Christ have been delivered from this present evil age.

q: With what is Paul amazed with the church in Galatia?
a: Paul is amazed that they are turning so quickly to a different gospel.

q: How many true gospels are there?
a: There is only one true gospel, the gospel of Christ.

q: What does Paul say should happen to anyone proclaiming a different gospel than the gospel of Christ?
a: Paul says anyone proclaiming a different gospel should be cursed.

q: Servants of Christ must seek the approval of whom first?
a: Servants of Christ must seek the approval of God first.

q: How did Paul receive the knowledge of the gospel of Christ?
a: Paul received the gospel of Christ by revelation from Jesus Christ directly to himself.

q: What was Paul doing in his life before he received the revelation of the gospel of Christ?
a: Paul was following Judaism zealously, persecuting the church of God and destroying it.

q: When did God choose Paul to be his apostle?
a: God was pleased to choose Paul from his mother’s womb to be his apostle.

q: For what purpose did God choose Paul as his apostle?
a: God chose Paul as his apostle so that Paul would proclaim Christ among the Gentiles.

q: Where did Paul finally meet some of the other apostles?
a: Finally, Paul went to Jerusalem and met the apostles Cephas and James.

q: What were the churches in Judea hearing about Paul?
a: The churches in Judea were hearing that Paul, who once persecuted the church, was now proclaiming the faith.

q: What did Paul do when he went up to Jerusalem after 14 years?
a: Paul spoke privately to the leaders of the church, explaining to them the gospel that he was proclaiming.

q: What was Titus, a Gentile, not required to do?
a: Titus was not required to be circumcised.

q: What did the false brothers desire to do?
a: The false brothers desired to make Paul and his companions slaves to the law.

q: Did the leaders of the church in Jerusalem change Paul’s message?
a: No, they added nothing to Paul’s message.

q: To whom was Paul primarily sent to proclaim the gospel?
a: Paul was primarily sent to the uncircumcised, the Gentiles, to proclaim the gospel.

q: To whom was Peter primarily sent to proclaim the gospel?
a: Peter was primarily sent to the circumcised, the Jews, to proclaim the gospel.

q: How did the leaders in Jerusalem show their approval of Paul’s ministry?
a: The leaders in Jerusalem gave Paul and Barnabas the right hand of fellowship to show their approval.

q: What error did Peter make when he came to Antioch?
a: Peter stopped eating with the Gentiles, because he feared the men who had been circumcised.

q: What did Paul ask Cephas in front of everyone?
a: Paul asked Cephas how he could force Gentiles to live like Jews when Cephas was living like a Gentile.

q: Paul said that no one is justified by what?
a: Paul said that no one is justified by the works of the law.

q: How is a person justified before God?
a: A person is justified before God by faith in Christ Jesus.

q: If someone returns to trying to follow the law after having faith in Christ, what does Paul say he has actually become?
a: Paul says he shows himself actually to be a law breaker.

q: Who did Paul say now lived in him?
a: Paul said that Christ now lived in him.

q: What does Paul say the Son of God did for him?
a: Paul says the Son of God loved him and gave himself for Paul.

q: How was Abraham considered righteous before God?
a: Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.

q: Who are the sons of Abraham?
a: Those who believe God are the sons of Abraham.

q: The scripture foresaw that the Gentiles would be justified in what way?
a: The scripture foresaw that the Gentiles would be justified by faith.

q: Those who rely on the works of the law to be justified are under what?
a: Those who rely on the works of the law to be justified are under a curse.

q: How many people have been justified by God through the works of the law?
a: No one has been justified through the works of the law.

q: Why did Christ redeem us by becoming a curse for us?
a: Christ redeemed us by becoming a curse for us so that the blessing upon Abraham might come to the Gentiles.

q: Who was the “descendant” that was spoken of in the promise to Abraham?
a: The “descendant” spoken of in the promise to Abraham was Christ.

q: Did the coming of the Jewish law 430 years after Abraham void the promise God made to Abraham?
a: No, the law did not void the promise made to Abraham.

q: Why then was there the law?
a: The law came because of transgressions until Abraham’s descendant came.

q: What did the law in scripture imprison everyone under?
a: The law in scripture imprisoned everyone under sin.

q: How are we released from the imprisonment of the law?
a: We are released from the imprisonment of the law by faith in Christ Jesus.

q: Who has been clothed in Christ?
a: All who have been baptized into Christ have been clothed in Christ.

q: What different kinds of persons are made one in Christ Jesus?
a: Jews, Greeks, slaves, free, male, and female are all made one in Christ Jesus.

q: How does the heir of an estate live while he is a child?
a: The heir lives like a slave under guardians and trustees until the time set by his father.

q: What did God do at the right time in history?
a: At the right time, God sent forth his Son to redeem those under the law.

q: How did God bring children who were under the law into his family?
a: God adopted as sons the children who were under the law.

q: What does God send forth into the hearts of his children?
a: God sends forth the Spirit of his Son into the hearts of his children.

q: Before we know God, to whom are we slaves?
a: Before we know God, we are slaves to the spirits that rule the world, who are not gods at all.

q: As he sees the Galatians turning back, what does Paul fear for them?
a: Paul fears that the Galatians will become slaves again, and that he has labored in vain over them.

q: Paul was perplexed that the Galatians were returning to what?
a: Paul was perplexed that the Galatians were returning again to the ruling spirits of the world.

q: When Paul first came to the Galatians, what problem did he have?
a: When Paul first came to the Galatians, he had a physical illness.

q: Despite Paul’s problem, how did the Galatians receive him?
a: Despite Paul’s problem, the Galatians received Paul as an angel of God, as Christ Jesus.

q: Who are the false teachers in Galatia trying to separate?
a: The false teachers are trying to separate the Galatians from Paul.

q: Under what are the false teachers trying to put the Galatians?
a: The false teachers are trying to put the Galatians back under the law.

q: From which two kinds of women did Abraham have two sons?
a: Abraham had two sons, one from a slave woman and one from a free woman.

q: Who is the symbolic mother of Paul and the believing Galatians?
a: The Jerusalem above, the free woman, is the symbolic mother of Paul and the believing Galatians.

q: Are believers in Christ children of the flesh or children of the promise?
a: Believers in Christ are children of the promise.

q: Who persecutes the children of the promise?
a: The children of the flesh persecute the children of the promise.

q: With whom do the children of the slave woman not inherit?
a: The children of the slave woman do not inherit along with the children of the free woman.

q: Are believers in Christ children of the slave woman or children of the free woman?
a: Believers in Christ are children of the free woman.

q: For what purpose has Christ set us free?
a: For freedom Christ has set us free.

q: What did Paul warn the Galatians would happen if they became circumcised?
a: Paul said that if the Galatians became circumcised, Christ would not benefit them in any way.

q: What did Paul warn would happen to all the Galatians who would seek to be justified by following the law?
a: Paul warned that all the Galatians who would seek to be justified by following the law would be alienated from Christ and would fall away from grace.

q: As opposed to circumcision and uncircumcised, what is the only thing that means anything in Christ Jesus?
a: In Christ Jesus, only faith working through love means anything.

q: Of what is Paul confident regarding the one who has confused the Galatians about the gospel?
a: Paul is confident that the one who has confused the Galatians about the gospel will bear God’s judgment.

q: Paul says that proclaiming circumcision does what?
a: Paul says that in proclaiming circumcision, the stumbling block of the cross would be destroyed.

q: How are believers not to use their freedom in Christ?
a: Believers are to not use their freedom in Christ as an opportunity for the flesh.

q: How are believers to use their freedom in Christ?
a: Believers are to use their freedom in Christ to serve one another in love.

q: The whole law is fulfilled in what one commandment?
a: The whole law is fulfilled in the commandment, “You must love your neighbor as yourself.”

q: How can believers not fulfill the lust of the flesh?
a: Believers can live by the Spirit, and thus, not fulfill the lust of the flesh.

q: What two things are opposed to each other within the believer?
a: The Spirit and the flesh are opposed to each other within the believer.

q: What are three examples of works of the flesh?
a: Three examples of works of the flesh are any three of the following list: sexual immorality, impurity, lustfulness, idolatry, sorcery, hostility, strife, jealousy, outbursts of anger, rivalry, dissension, sectarian division, envy, drunkenness, and drunken riots.

q: What will those who practice the works of the flesh not receive?
a: Those who practice the works of the flesh will not inherit the kingdom of God.

q: What is the fruit of the Spirit?
a: The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith, gentleness, and self-control.

q: Those who belong to Christ Jesus have done what with the flesh and its passions?
a: Those who belong to Christ Jesus have crucified the flesh and its passions.

q: What should those who are spiritual do if a man is caught in some transgression?
a: Those who are spiritual should restore that man in a spirit of gentleness.

q: For what danger must those who are spiritual watch out?
a: Those who are spiritual must watch out that they are not also tempted.

q: How do believers fulfill the law of Christ?
a: Believers fulfill the law of Christ by carrying one another’s burdens.

q: How can a person have something in himself to be proud of regarding his work?
a: A person can have something in himself to be proud of by examining his own work, without comparing himself to anyone else.

q: What must one who is taught the word do with his teacher?
a: One who is taught the word must share all good things with his teacher.

q: What happens to whatever a man spiritually plants?
a: Whatever a man spiritually plants he will harvest.

q: What does a man harvest who plants to his own flesh?
a: A man who plants to his own flesh harvests destruction out of his flesh.

q: What does a man harvest who plants to the Spirit?
a: Out of the Spirit a man who plants to the Spirit harvests eternal life.

q: If a believer does not give up and continues doing good, what will he receive?
a: A believer who continues doing good will reap a harvest.

q: To whom should believers especially do good?
a: Believers should especially do good to those of the household of faith.

q: What is the motivation of those who want to compel the believers to be circumcised?
a: Those who want to compel the believers to be circumcised do not want to be persecuted for the cross of Christ.

q: Of what did Paul say he was proud?
a: Paul said that he was proud of the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ.

q: Instead of circumcision or uncircumcision, what is important?
a: What is important is a new creation.

q: Upon whom does Paul wish peace and mercy?
a: Paul wishes peace and mercy upon those who live by the rule of the new creation and upon the Israel of God.

q: What did Paul carry on his body?
a: Paul carried the marks of Jesus on his body.
